questions.question: On a freeway, you miss your turn or exit. What should you do?

options.text: Make a quick turn from your lane.
Stop and back up.
Keep driving until you find the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until you find the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Go to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: What safety restraints work best in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
A lap and shoulder belt plus an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lap and shoulder belt plus an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash and greatly reduce serious injury. Airbags used with safety belts provide extra protection in front-end crashes. You should wear both shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: How can you fight fatigue on a long trip?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: To prevent fatigue on a long trip, stop every two hours for a break. If you feel drowsy, pull off the road to a safe place and nap, or find a place to stay for the night.

questions.question: How can you make sure your health does not make you drive unsafely?

options.text: Stay physically fit and have regular health checkups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Your health affects your ability to drive safely. Drivers must know their physical limits and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you do if you are in a serious car crash?

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is injured.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: In a crash, move your car off the road and stop if you can. If anyone is hurt, call 911 and help them. You must report the crash to police if there is an injury, a death, or more than $1,000 in property damage (or more than $200 in damage to government property like signs or guardrails).

questions.question: Your car breaks down on a highway. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers and carefully exit the road. Get as far off the road as possible. Lift your hood so other drivers know your car is disabled.

questions.question: A tire blows out while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard immediately.
Keep the car straight and slow down by releasing the gas pedal.
Keep your current speed and drive straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slow down by releasing the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Release the gas pedal and do not brake until you have control. Once the car is steady, brake gently and pull off the road at a safe spot.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:

options.text: Speed up faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Look for a way around lowered gates.
Assume no trains are near and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert drivers that a train may be near. Obey all warning signs and never go around barriers or ignore the sign.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, make a clear path and stop. Slow down and safely pull to the side of the road. If you are in heavy traffic directly in front of the emergency vehicle, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them from crossing against the light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians and other cars that may be in the intersection, even when you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: Smoking while driving:

options.text: Does not affect driving ability.
Helps keep drivers alert.
Is a distraction.
Is not a distraction.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving distracts you. You may take your hands off the wheel or your eyes off the road.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Winding road.
Pedestrian crossing.
Low ground railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low ground railroad crossing. Railroad tracks cross the road at a steep slope. The bottom of low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the narrow bridge ahead.
The bridge ahead is one-way only.
The bridge ahead fits only one car at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck. Drive with caution.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.
Hill ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. This tells other drivers what you plan to do and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting or reacting in anger:

options.text: Do not make eye contact.
Do not use hand gestures.
Distance yourself from the situation.
All of these.

questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, stay away from the situation. Avoid eye contact and do not make gestures that could provoke them. Slow down, move over, or do whatever is safe to keep yourself out of danger.

questions.question: When you see a red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: A red traffic light means you must come to a complete stop. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if no sign prohibits it.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Your driver's license.
Proof of registration.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When stopped, you must show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You must have all three documents in your vehicle when driving.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the steering wheel. Tell passengers to keep their hands in view. Stay in your vehicle unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver's license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Get some coffee.
Open your window.
Stop driving.
Turn on the radio.

questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: What do highway markings do?

options.text: They are usually not important.
They are only found in construction zones.
They give information to drivers.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers. They show drivers where to position their vehicles, tell drivers where it is safe to pass, and warn drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: You are in an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Stop right away.
Help injured people.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: In an accident, stop your vehicle immediately. If possible, move it out of traffic. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Try to stop serious bleeding by pressing on the wound. Wait for emergency help to arrive.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not lower your BAC or reduce alcohol's effects. These things may help you stay awake, but they cannot change your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: How can you best avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Drive slowly on wet or slushy roads.
Watch for standing water and puddles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, cars need more distance to stop and may skid when turning quickly. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but hurts your judgment.
It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either.
It hurts driving skills but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms many skills needed for safe driving. It slows your reaction time and hurts your vision. It also makes you misjudge speed and distance, lowers your caution, and makes you more likely to take dangerous risks.
